title: Tenochtitlan Was Cleaner Than London
hook: Tenochtitlan had 1,000 public street cleaners and dual fresh aqueducts.

scenes.text: When Spanish conquistadors first entered Tenochtitlan in 1519, they were stunned by a city far cleaner than Paris, London, or Madrid.
scenes.imagePrompt: Immaculate paved stone causeway leading across turquoise Lake Texcoco into the gleaming white pyramids of Tenochtitlan. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: When Spanish conquistadors first entered Tenochtitlan in 1519, they were stunned by a city far cleaner than Paris, London, or Madrid.

scenes.text: While European cities threw raw chamber pots directly into dirt streets, Tenochtitlan employed one thousand dedicated municipal street sweepers.
scenes.imagePrompt: Spotless stone marketplace plaza swept clean with reed brooms under clear blue skies beside whitewashed adobe walls. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: While European cities threw raw chamber pots directly into dirt streets, Tenochtitlan employed one thousand dedicated municipal street sweepers.

scenes.text: Fresh mountain spring water flowed into city centers through the Chapultepec aqueduct: twin pipes engineered so one could be cleaned while water flowed.
scenes.imagePrompt: Double stone aqueduct bridge crossing turquoise lake waters with clean mountain water flowing through smooth mortar channels. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Fresh mountain spring water flowed into city centers through the Chapultepec aqueduct: twin pipes engineered so one could be cleaned while water flowed.

scenes.text: Aztecs bathed twice daily in freshwater canals or private dome steam baths called 'temazcals', using saponin-rich soaproot plants.

scenes.voicedText: Aztecs bathed twice daily in freshwater canals or private dome steam baths called 'temazcals', using saponin-rich soaproot plants.

scenes.text: They brushed their teeth with charred charcoal and wild pepper bark, and chewed aromatic 'chicle' tree sap to sweeten their breath.

scenes.voicedText: They brushed their teeth with charred charcoal and wild pepper bark, and chewed aromatic 'chicle' tree sap to sweeten their breath.

scenes.text: Aztecs found Spanish soldiers' body odor completely repulsive! Did you know the Aztecs invented natural chewing gum?
